A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same VCA paper. Their methods, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original VCA benchmark results, component ablations, reward analyses, and failure cases in Sections 4–5 and Appendices 9–10.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and reports revised open-source experiments plus new buffer-size and image-reward comparisons.

M1.justification: The core tree-search, reward, and memory procedures remain unchanged. However, the open-source implementation replaces v1's Qwen2-VL-7B visual assistant and Qwen2.5-7B text-based selector with a single Qwen2-VL-72B model serving exploration and reward roles, removing the intermediate visual-to-text handoff.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate EgoSchema, LVBench, MMBench-Video, and VideoMME's long split. The revised model configurations and added ablations introduce no distinct dataset, task, population, or input-environment coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds the image-reward variant to the open-source EgoSchema comparison in Table 5. Figure 1 also explicitly plots a Qwen2-VL CoT point, although its relationship to the tabulated uniform-sampling results is unclear. Established VideoAgent, VideoTree, LVNet, and video-model comparator families are retained.

E3.justification: The open-source comparison is substantially reconfigured: the two-model 7B setup becomes Qwen2-VL-72B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4, the memory buffer increases from 8 to 16 frames, and uniform-sampling settings change from 16/32 to 8/32 frames. V2 also adds GPU-hour evaluation, buffer-size controls, and an image-relevance control. The principal GPT-4o benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds two focused diagnostics: LVBench sensitivity to 8/16/32-frame memory buffers and an EgoSchema comparison using endpoint-image relevance instead of inferred segment semantics. Existing reward/tree-search ablations, oracle-reward analysis, selection distributions, exploration examples, and appendix failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark accuracy. Figure 5's fitted segment-distance distributions and associated reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The open-source result block is replaced: v1 Table 4 reports VCA at 62.4% with 9.1 frames, whereas v2 Table 5 reports 75.2% with 16.9 frames under different model and buffer settings. V2 adds buffer-size accuracies of 38.9/41.3/43.2%, image-reward accuracy of 74.0%, and GPU-hour results. These are not same-setting performance gains; the principal GPT-4o and appendix benchmark scores are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of segments, reward history, candidate sets, and memory updates are retained, as is Algorithm 1. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and v2 introduces no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central contribution. The introduction refines the efficiency contribution from using the least observed frames to using fewer frames with comparable or lower computational cost, and makes the distinction between segment exploration and image-based retrieval more explicit.

C2.justification: V2 interprets buffer-size gains as benefiting from a broader reasoning window, acknowledges testing only up to 32 frames, and attributes the image-reward deficit to losing segment semantics. It removes the earlier discussion of small-model instruction-following difficulties. The existing failure-mode explanations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the quantized 72B checkpoint, identifies a single H100 for timing, and adds captioning-cost estimates. Its main-text baseline description now agrees with the Qwen captioning/GPT-4o reasoning arrangement already documented in v1 Appendix 8.2. This correction does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. Appendix prompts, other baseline hyperparameters, and access links are retained.

R1.justification: V2 removes citations to Working Memory, CoVLM, FlexAttention, RILA, and 3D-VLA. It strengthens the specific contrast with VideoTree's captioning cost and frame-selection approach, while retaining the broader related-work organization and research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 revises introductory motivation, trims the human-cognition explanation, rewrites the open-source subsection, and swaps the order of the open-source and exploration-behavior analyses. Most methodological prose and appendix text remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces its LVBench panel with an open-source GPU-hour comparison, and Figure 2 replaces the human-reasoning illustration with a comparison against prior methods. V2 adds a buffer-size table and an image-reward row, with local table and figure relocations. The remaining pipeline, prompt, trajectory, and failure-case visuals are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens support for memory capacity and segment-based reasoning through targeted ablations, and corrects the misleading main-text baseline description. The common-model open-source comparison also improves evaluation clarity. These gains are limited: the smaller-model results disappear, changed settings prevent direct performance-gain claims, and Figure 1's open-source accuracies are not fully reconciled with Table 5.
